subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Future of Human-Robot Interaction
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Future of Human-Robot Interaction.

hook.text: Robots are leaving factories and entering homes, hospitals, and streets. The rules of interaction are being rewritten.

buildup.text: Social robots use facial expressions, gestures, and voice to communicate. People naturally respond to them as social beings.

discovery.text: Exoskeletons merge robot and human. Powered frames amplify the wearer's strength and restore mobility to paralyzed limbs.

twist.text: People form emotional bonds with robots. Soldiers mourn fallen bomb-disposal robots. Children treat toy robots as friends.

climax.text: As robots become more capable, society must decide where to draw lines — in care, warfare, privacy, and autonomy.

punchline.text: The hardest part of robotics isn't the robot. It's the relationship.

quiz.question: What does the emotional bonding between humans and robots suggest?
options: Robots have achieved genuine consciousness and feelings
People naturally treat social robots as beings, raising ethical questions about their use
Emotional bonding is a design flaw that engineers are trying to eliminate
